title: Retain wider terminal Uniform merge experiment
question: Can a larger bounded fan-in avoid a full intermediate merge on a constrained terminal Uniform job?
summary: Keep the opt-in Linux merge ceiling. Median elapsed fell 20.59% and managed temporary writes fell 49.39% at 8 GiB; managed temporary files and CLI RSS increased.

workloads: 8 GiB Uniform Shuffle to eight exact Balanced parts, 197 runs, 256 MiB engine setting, one worker, 1 GiB cgroup without swap.

validation.summary: Three matched complete pairs with field, ID conservation, exact quota, serialized cap, metadata and cleanup checks. Separate 256-descriptor low-limit fallback and full diagnostic verified. Retained source passed formatting, default and all-feature Clippy and workspace tests, portable-core WASM check, WASI feature compile, and default native release build on the Linux host.

limitations: One synthetic WSL2/ext4 input shape with uncontrolled host backing cache.
Descriptor threshold is not global admission. Managed temporary-file count is not a process descriptor census.
Working reservations, CLI RSS, and cgroup memory describe different resource bounds.
exclusions: Small preflight, low-descriptor fallback control, structural diagnostic and excluded warmup.
reopen_when: Require varied data, scale transfer and native workload calibration before proposing wider activation.
